en: 10. The Pairs on the Faculties (Indriyayamaka) 10.3.
The Section on Full Understanding (Pariññāvāra) 10.3.1.
The Section on the Present (Paccuppannavāra)
10.3.1.1. Positive (Anuloma) He who fully understands the eye-faculty, does he also fully understand the ear-faculty? Yes.
Or, he who fully understands the ear-faculty, does he also fully understand the eye-faculty? Yes.
Is one who fully understands the eye-faculty abandoning the faculty of mental grief? No.
Or again, is one who abandons the faculty of mental grief fully understanding the eye-faculty? No.
Is one who fully understands the eye-faculty developing the “I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown” faculty? No.
Or, is it that whoever develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya) also fully understands the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya)? No.
Is it that whoever fully understands the eye-faculty also develops the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? Yes.
Or, is it that whoever develops the faculty of final knowledge also fully understands the eye-faculty?

Two types of persons develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*), yet they do not fully understand the eye-faculty (*cakkhundriya*). One who possesses the supreme path (*aggamaggasamaṅgī*) both develops the faculty of final knowledge and fully understands the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the eye-faculty realizes the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever realizes the faculty of one who has already known fully understands the eye-faculty? No. (Based on the eye-faculty.)
Is it the case that whoever abandons the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" abandons the faculty of mental distress? No.
Is it the case that whoever abandons the faculty of mental distress develops the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)? Yes.
Or again, does he who develops the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) abandon the faculty of mental distress (*domanassindriya*)?

Two types of persons develop the faculty of final knowledge, yet they do not abandon the faculty of mental distress. One who possesses the path of the non-returner (*anāgāmimagga*) develops the faculty of final knowledge and abandons the faculty of mental distress.
Does he who abandons the faculty of mental distress realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*)? No.
Or, does one who realizes the faculty of one-who-has-known abandon the faculty of mental displeasure? No. (Based on the faculty of mental displeasure.
Does one who develops the faculty of "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" develop the faculty of final knowledge? No.
Or, does one who develops the faculty of final knowledge develop the faculty of "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown"? No.
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown” realizes the faculty of one who has known? No.

Or else, is it the case that whoever realizes the faculty of one who has known develops the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown”? No. (Based on the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown.
Is it the case that whoever develops the faculty of final knowledge realizes the faculty of one who has known? No.
Or, does he who realizes the *aññātāvindriya* (the faculty of one who has already known) develop the *aññindriya* (the faculty of final knowledge)? No. (Based on the *aññindriya*.
10.3.1.2. Negative (Paccanīka):
Does he who does not fully understand the *cakkhundriya* (the eye-faculty) not abandon the *domanassindriya* (the faculty of mental grief)?
One who possesses the path of the non-returner (anāgāmimagga) does not fully understand the eye-faculty (cakkhundriya), yet he does not abandon the grief-faculty (domanassindriya).
With the exception of those two who possess the paths, all remaining persons neither fully understand the eye-faculty nor abandon the grief-faculty.
Or, is it the case that whoever does not abandon the grief-faculty does not fully understand the eye-faculty?
One who possesses the highest path (agga-maggasamaṅgī) does not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya), but he does not fail to fully understand the faculty of the eye (cakkhundriya).
With the exception of those two who possess the [first] two paths, all remaining persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor do they fully understand the faculty of the eye.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the faculty of the eye does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?
The person at the eighth stage does not fully understand the eye faculty, yet he does not fail to develop the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty.
With the exception of those two who possess the path, all remaining persons neither fully understand the eye faculty nor develop the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty.
Or, conversely: whoever does not develop the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty, does he not fully understand the eye faculty?
One who possesses the supreme path does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet he does not fail to fully understand the eye-faculty.

With the exception of those two types of persons possessing the paths, all remaining individuals neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor do they fully understand the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the faculty of the eye does not develop the faculty of final knowledge?

Two types of persons do not fully understand the faculty of the eye, yet they do not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge. With the exception of those three who possess the path, all remaining persons neither fully understand the faculty of the eye nor develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Or conversely, is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge does not fully understand the faculty of the eye? Yes, it is.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the eye-faculty does not realize the faculty of one who has already known?
Whoever realizes the fruit of the highest path (agga-phala) does not fully understand the eye-faculty, yet he does not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known.
With the exception of one possessing the highest path (aggamagga-samaṅgī) and the Arahant, all remaining persons [do not fully understand the eye-faculty].
They do not fully understand the faculty of one who has already known, nor do they realize it.
Or, is it the case that whoever does not realize the faculty of one who has already known also does not fully understand the eye-faculty?
One who possesses the path of the highest (agga-magga) does not realize the faculty of one who has already known, but he does not fail to fully understand the eye-faculty.

With the exception of one who possesses the highest path and an Arahant, all remaining persons neither realize the faculty of having known nor fully understand the eye-faculty. (Based on the eye-faculty.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental grief does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?

The person at the eighth stage (aṭṭhamaka) does not abandon the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya), yet it is not the case that he does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya).
With the exception of those two who possess the path (maggasamaṅgin), all remaining persons neither abandon the faculty of mental grief nor develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Or conversely: whoever does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" does not abandon the faculty of mental grief?
One who possesses the path of the non-returner does not cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet he does not abandon the faculty of mental grief.
With the exception of two individuals possessing the paths, all remaining persons neither cultivate the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor do they abandon the faculty of mental grief.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)?

Two types of persons do not abandon the faculty of mental distress, yet they do not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge. With the exception of those three who possess the path (maggasamaṅgino), all remaining persons neither abandon the faculty of mental distress nor develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Or conversely, is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge does not abandon the faculty of mental distress? Yes, it is.
Is it the case that whoever does not abandon the faculty of mental distress (domanassindriya) does not realize the faculty of one who has known (aññātāvindriya)?
Whoever realizes the fruit of the highest attainment (aggaphala) does not abandon the faculty of mental distress, yet it is not the case that they do not realize the faculty of one who has known.
With the exception of those possessing the path of the non-returner (anāgāmimagga-samaṅgin) and the Arahant, all remaining persons [do not abandon the faculty of mental distress].
They do not abandon [the faculty of] one who has already known, nor do they realize it.
Or rather: does one who does not realize the faculty of one who has already known not abandon the faculty of mental distress?
One who possesses the path of non-returning does not realize the faculty of one who has already known, yet he does not fail to abandon the faculty of mental distress.

With the exception of one who possesses the path of the non-returner and an Arahant, all remaining persons neither realize the faculty of "I-have-known" nor abandon the faculty of mental grief. (Based on the faculty of mental grief.
He who does not develop the faculty of "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" does not develop the faculty of final knowledge. Is that so?
Three possessors of the path do not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet they do not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge.
With the exception of the four possessors of the path, all remaining persons neither develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" nor do they develop the faculty of final knowledge.
Or again, does he who does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya) not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (anaññātaññassāmītindriya)?
The person at the eighth stage (aṭṭhamaka) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge, but he does not fail to develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
With the exception of those possessing the four paths, all remaining persons neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor do they develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" does not realize the faculty of one who has already known?
Whoever realizes the fruit of Arhatship does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," yet he does not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known.
With the exception of the person at the eighth stage and the Arhat, all remaining persons [either] do not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" and...
They do not develop the faculty of one who has already known and they do not realize it.
Or, is it the case that whoever does not realize the faculty of one who has already known does not develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?
One who is at the eighth stage (the *aṣṭamaka*) does not realize the faculty of one who has already known, yet he does not fail to develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."

With the exception of the eighth person and the Arahat, all remaining persons neither realize the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*) nor develop the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (*anaññātaññassāmītindriya*). (Based on the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
Is it the case that whoever does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (*aññindriya*) does not realize the faculty of one who has already known?

He who realizes the fruit of Arhatship (aggaphala) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya), yet he does not fail to realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya).
With the exception of those possessing the three paths and the Arhat, all remaining persons neither develop the faculty of final knowledge nor realize the faculty of one who has already known.
Or, is it the case that whoever does not realize the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya) does not develop the faculty of final knowledge (aññindriya)?
Those possessing the three paths do not realize the faculty of one who has already known, yet they do not fail to develop the faculty of final knowledge.
With the exception of those possessing the three paths and the Arahant, all remaining persons neither realize the faculty of one who has already known...
They realize [the fruit] but do not develop the faculty of final knowledge. (Based on the faculty of final knowledge.)
